structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E046. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2; fresh seeds 13-22 gave 0.7525. Identical-code reruns (E038 0.7525, E043 0.7497) show rebuild noise of about 0.3 pp on a 3-seed mean, so a 3-seed read near 0.753 is a coin flip. Population mean is about 0.752, leaving about 0.2 pp of headroom over the 0.75 bar.

Mechanisms, with supporting experiments:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked the freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, wd, LS), so averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free up to about 30% of steps at 20 px (E026, E033). E040 saved 0.12 s and cost 0.06-0.28 pp. E041 (12-step trim) cost about 0.2 pp. E045 (smaller early batch) cost +0.2 s and gained nothing measurable.
4. Backward truncation was the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 (freeze at 60%) saved 0.25 s but cost 0.38 pp. E039 and E042 saved only 0.03-0.05 s. E046 (group-2 freeze for the last 10%) saved 0.24 s and held accuracy at 0.7540. That is larger than my 0.06 s estimate, so group-2 backward is costlier than its MAC share, or the saving includes other overhead. Backward in the frozen window is the cheap lever, but accuracy was not significantly separated from noise.
5. Loss-based dropping (E031) and fewer steps cost about 1.5-2.3 s per pp, about the same rate as the epoch dial.
6. Noise: 3-seed accuracy std is about 0.15-0.2 pp, and any RNG or step-count change reshuffles it. Time noise is about 0.5%, or about ±0.03 s near 5.3 s.

Misses: E046 time (predicted 5.27, measured 5.08), because I under-valued the saving per frozen step. E043 was a rebuild-noise miss. Time-neutral boosters were over-predicted.

Unsure: whether the E046 saving is real or partly a time artifact, and whether it transfers to the PCIe judge, since it is bandwidth-bound. I also don't know whether padding to 32 channels gives more than 2%, or whether a profile finds a lever.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change, so the numbers are just a rerun of E036. The profile will probably show the stem and non-GEMM kernels taking a large share, but this is not a pass/fail test.
E031's 10% drop gave -0.63 s and -0.27 pp, so 5% should give about -0.2 s and -0.1 pp. That is within noise, and the scatter and topk overhead eats a little of the saving.
Padding to 32 channels may speed up the Cin=24 conv a little, but the whitening output is only about 13% of step FLOPs. The expected gain is under 2%, and the rebuild gives accuracy noise.

cruxes: Is E046's 0.24 s saving from a 10% group-2 freeze real, and does it hold on seeds 13-32? If so, a longer or deeper cascade is the best remaining lever.
What does a profile of the tip show for group-1 conv1 (Cin=24) and the non-GEMM kernels? Padding in I073 is worth more than 2% only if conv1 is inefficient.
What is the population mean accuracy of the tip on unselected seeds? If it is below 0.752, no further time cut is safe.
